subject: Clarifying subprocessor liability & transfer-addendum (DPA / SCCs)

Subject: DPA follow-up — clarification on subprocessor liability and SCCs

Diego / Ben — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal reviewed the current DPA and flagged two items we need clearer language on before we can circulate to security for final signoff: 

1) Subprocessor liability: our standard asks the vendor to take on a liability cap carveout where subcontractor-caused breaches are not subject to the vendor's general cap for the specific subset of regulated data. We saw your base DPA includes a flow-down but stops short of the carveout. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a carveout for breaches caused by subcontractors processing regulated health data?

2) SCCs & transfer-addendum: we need explicit confirmation of which SCCs variant you're adopting and whether the order form will reference a transfer-impact addendum for non-EEA hosting. Attached is an excerpt of the clauses our counsel prefers (MediSphere_SCCs_Excerpt.pdf).

We've attached a short subprocessor matrix request (subprocessor_matrix.xlsx). If you can share a redline against Redwood_DPA_v3 by end of day tomorrow, that will keep our procurement timeline intact.

Thanks,
Elena Novak
Corporate Counsel — MediSphere

Subject: Re: DPA follow-up — clarification on subprocessor liability and SCCs

Hi all — thanks for the context. I've reviewed MediSphere's SCC excerpt and drafted a focused redline (attached: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.docx). Highlights of our position below: 

- Subprocessor liability carveout: Redwood can accept a limited carveout where liability caps do not apply for breaches directly caused by a subprocessor's gross negligence or willful misconduct that results in unauthorized access to regulated health data (PHI-equivalent). We propose: carveout limited in time (remediation period), capped to a per-incident remediation fund, and requiring reasonable mitigation steps by Redwood and the subprocessor.

- Flow-down and audit: we will flow down confidentiality/security obligations to subprocessors and commit to providing MediSphere with SOC-related summaries and a reasonable audit process (redacted). We will not provide on-site audits for all subprocessors — propose a shared third-party audit path.

- SCCs & transfer-addendum: Redwood will adopt the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (2021) for controller-processor relationships and will include a transfer-impact addendum in the order form when any personal data is processed outside the EEA. We will mark the order form template to call out the selected SCCs variant and include a short transfer-impact questionnaire that references hosting region and KMS/crypto controls.

I've also added commentary where MediSphere's draft requested broader indemnity language — flagged those for negotiation (see para 6 redline comments).

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.docx
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.docx
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@medisphere.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up — clarification on subprocessor liability and SCCs

Laura — thanks for the quick redline. A few follow-ups from our security and procurement teams: 

1) Can you confirm the operational gating for the carveout — specifically, how will MediSphere be notified of a subprocessor breach and what SLAs for notification/remediation will Redwood require from its subprocessor? Our security policy asks for 72-hour initial notification for incidents involving regulated data.

2) Regarding on-site audits: MediSphere prefers the option for an on-site inspection (or equivalent controlled remote audit) for subprocessors that process EEA regulated data. If Redwood can offer a limited on-site right for material subprocessors (with NDA and scoped audit plan), that would satisfy our risk team.

3) SCCs: procurement asked to confirm that the transfer-impact addendum will include a plain-English summary of transfer risk and the mitigation controls (hosting region, encryption at-rest/in-transit, KMS locality).

If you can confirm the notification SLA and audit path and post the updated redline with a short paragraph for the transfer-impact summary, we can route to security and aim to close next week.

Best,
Elena
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@medisphere.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up — clarification on subprocessor liability and SCCs

Elena — appreciate the specific asks; quick operational answers below and we'll incorporate into the updated redline by Monday morning: 

• Notification SLA: Redwood requires subprocessors to notify Redwood within 24 hours of becoming aware of an incident affecting regulated data. Redwood will notify customers within 48 hours with an initial incident summary and follow up with a remediation timeline. We can align the contract language to commit to a 72-hour initial notification to MediSphere if that is your firm requirement.

• Audits: For material subprocessors (defined in the DPA as those processing >10% of a customer's regulated data or with access to keys), Redwood will offer either (1) a scoped on-site audit with reasonable advance notice and NDA, or (2) a shared third-party audit report (SOC2/ISO) plus a controlled remote review. We'll add a clause that permits MediSphere to request an on-site review for material subprocessors subject to Redwood's operational approval (to avoid high-frequency requests).

• Transfer-impact summary: we'll add a plain-language summary box to the transfer-addendum that lists hosting region(s), whether keys are region-bound, encryption at-rest/in-transit, and the SCCs variant adopted.

Next steps: Laura will produce an updated redline (Redwood_DPA_v4) capturing these commitments; Diego — we'll coordinate DocuSign flow once legal signs off.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Privacy & Trust Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: subprocessor_matrix.xlsx (will be shared by EOD Monday)
